patch.objective: Computing ethics: intellectual property, privacy, and computer crime

sources.cite: ACM/IEEE-CS/AAAI, Computer Science Curricula 2023 (CS2023), knowledge areas (SEP: Society, Ethics, and the Profession)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the report's first part: 17 knowledge areas, among them SEP: Society, Ethics, and the Profession; the fetch reached the table of contents, not the topic lists. The CMPCBS course cites CS2023 and its unit's open textbooks (dated 2026-11-11, REQ-245). The course's unit cites CS2023 knowledge units SEP-Privacy and SEP-Security. The case: a lead asks for shared admin credentials and audit logging off on a patient records server; due diligence, a refusal with a legitimate route, escalation only through the documented channel.

sources.cite: ISC2, CC Certification Exam Outline (effective 2026-09-01), Domain 1: Security Principles (ISC2 Code of Ethics)
sources.note: Headings read on the outline page and its English PDF on 2026-11-14 for REQ-270 and not re-read; Domain 1 lists the code of ethics among the security principles. The course's objective wording is its own.

sources.cite: ISC2 Code of Ethics: preamble and the four mandatory canons
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the code's page. Canon I 'Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure'; Canon II 'Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally'; Canon III 'Provide diligent and competent service to principals'; Canon IV 'Advance and protect the profession'. The page does not rank the canons. Members who observe a breach by a member must follow the complaint procedure (complaints in writing, as a sworn affidavit). Learner-facing text in the sim names 'your professional code of ethics', not the certifying body.
